en: Paccuppannātītavāra (The Chapter on the Present and the Past)
Is it the case that whoever fully understands the truth of suffering has abandoned the truth of the origin? No.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever has abandoned the truth of the origin has fully understood the truth of suffering? No.
Is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the truth of suffering has not abandoned the truth of the origin?
An Arahant does not fully understand the truth of suffering, yet he has not failed to abandon the truth of the origin.

With the exception of one who possesses the highest path (the Arahant) and the Arahant himself, all remaining persons neither fully understand the truth of suffering nor have they abandoned the truth of the origin.
Or, conversely: whoever has not abandoned the truth of the origin does not fully understand the truth of suffering?
One who possesses the highest path has not abandoned the truth of origination, yet it is not the case that he does not fully understand the truth of suffering.
With the exception of one who possesses the highest path and an Arhat, all remaining persons have neither abandoned the truth of origination nor fully understood the truth of suffering.
